summary: Iteration 20 — Live-stream twin (/api/live/*) + companion_desktop path migration. Wrote 33 new tests covering handle validation, claim/idempotent/collision, settings PATCH semantics, public profile/recent endpoints, SSE hello receipt, publish_turn pub/sub semantics (enabled/private_mode/cross-user isolation), and desktop zip rebuild from new in-backend path. Also ran all 4 regression suites (iter16-19); 3 pre-existing tests had hardcoded /app/companion_desktop paths that broke due to the migration — patched the test paths to prefer /app/backend/companion_desktop with fallback. Final: 73/73 passing (33 iter20 + 40 regression).
critical_code_review_comments: SSE cross-process testing limitation noted: in-process `publish_turn` from the pytest process can never reach the running uvicorn process's BUS (separate Python interpreters → separate module-level _Bus instances). The end-to-end publish→SSE event chain is therefore validated in two halves: (a) HTTP SSE `hello` event is received from the running server, (b) publish_turn → BUS.subscribe semantics (incl. enabled/private_mode/cross-user isolation) are validated via direct in-process subscription. This is documented in the test. If full E2E coverage is needed, the publish would have to be triggered via an HTTP endpoint (e.g., POST to /api/twin/chat).
routers/live.py: BUS is in-memory only — explicitly noted in module docstring that multi-worker deployments require Redis. Current single-worker setup is fine.

routers/live.py:228 `viewer_count` is read-only at request time (BUS.subscriber_count) which is a process-local count — viewers connected to other workers won't be counted. Matches the in-memory bus design tradeoff.
routers/companion.py build_desktop_app_zip_bytes correctly tries /app/backend/companion_desktop first with /app/companion_desktop dev fallback — clean migration.
test_credentials: Mints fresh users + sessions per test via pymongo direct insert (prefixes u_live_*). Cleaned up in teardown_module.
seed_data_creation: Per-test users in `users` + `user_sessions`, ad-hoc rows in `live_profiles` and `conversations` (kind=companion_twin). All cleaned in teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter20 test file uses pytest-asyncio + httpx.AsyncClient(stream=True) for SSE. Motor binds to the event loop on first use, and pytest-asyncio creates a new loop per test → use the `_reset_motor_for_current_loop()` helper inside async tests before calling any code that touches `routers.live.db`. The SSE end-to-end publish chain (publish_turn → server SSE stream) is NOT testable cross-process; the test split is intentional. For iter17/18/19 regression tests, hardcoded /app/companion_desktop paths were patched to try /app/backend/companion_desktop first with dev fallback. publish_turn in routers/live.py and publish_avatar both consult live_profiles before publishing — silent drop semantics are tested.
rca of the issue: First test run had 5 SSE failures: (1) pytest-asyncio creates new event loop per function, but motor's AsyncIOMotorClient is bound to first loop → 'Event loop is closed' on subsequent tests. Fixed by re-instantiating AsyncIOMotorClient inside each async test and re-binding routers.live.db. (2) Cross-process publish_turn → SSE end-to-end is structurally impossible (test BUS ≠ server BUS) — restructured: test #1 only validates SSE hello receipt over HTTP; tests #2-5 validate publish_turn pub/sub semantics via local BUS.subscribe. Also fixed 3 regression failures from desktop path migration by adding dual-path fallback in 3 test files.
